headline: The Fed promises patience and shares jump 8 percent
text: Early in January Federal Reserve officials said the central bank could be 'patient' about further rate rises, and positive signals on trade with China followed. The S&P 500 rose 8% in January to 2,704.10, winning back most of December's loss. The numbers: the Fed's rate 2.4 percent. Inflation 2.0 percent. Unemployment 3.9 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1955 to January 2019
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Swiss pupils strike for the climate
text: On 17 and 18 January at least 45,000 students in Switzerland and Germany skipped school to protest against weak climate policies, following the Swedish schoolgirl Greta Thunberg, who began the school strikes outside her country's parliament. More strikes are planned.

headline: GE's cash flow beats fears
text: On 31 January General Electric reported fourth-quarter revenue up 5% to 33.3 billion dollars and 5.5 billion dollars of industrial free cash flow in the quarter, more than investors had feared after a year of bad news.
imageCaption: A GE90 jet engine, built by GE Aviation, on display

headline: Citigroup's profit beats the gloom
text: Citigroup reported fourth-quarter 2018 net income of $4.3 billion excluding a tax item and said it returned $18.4 billion to shareholders in 2018. After a 9% fall in the S&P 500 in December, stocks rebounded, and Citigroup's shares rose 24% in January.
imageCaption: 388 Greenwich Street, 2019

headline: eBay pays its first dividend
text: On January 29 eBay announced its first-ever dividend, 14 cents a share each quarter from March, and $4 billion more for share buybacks, planning to return about $7 billion to shareholders over two years. It has 179 million active buyers.
imageCaption: Paul Singer, 2013

headline: Tim Cook warns: China and fewer iPhone upgrades
text: On 2 January Tim Cook cut Apple's revenue forecast for the December quarter to about 84 billion dollars, below its earlier guidance, in a letter to investors. He blamed a much sharper slowdown in China than expected and fewer iPhone upgrades; sales outside the iPhone grew almost 19%.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019319000002/a8-kexhibit991122019.htm (Letter from Tim Cook to Apple investors, 2 January 2019, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Tim Cook, Apple's chief executive, at the White House
imageCredit: The White House from Washington, DC

headline: Bob Swan becomes permanent chief executive
text: On 31 January Intel named Bob Swan, its finance chief since 2016 and interim chief executive for seven months, as its seventh chief executive.

headline: Amazon drops its New York headquarters plan
text: On February 14 Amazon said it will not build its planned second headquarters in Queens, New York, after local opposition, and will concentrate on Arlington, Virginia, where it plans at least 25,000 jobs.

headline: Glencore caps its coal output
text: With its 2018 results on 20 February, Glencore committed to limit its coal production capacity broadly to current levels and to put its investment into commodities needed for the energy and transport transition, such as copper, cobalt and nickel.

headline: Paris court fines UBS 3.7 billion euros
text: On 20 February a Paris court convicted UBS of illegally soliciting clients in France and laundering the proceeds of tax fraud, and ordered it to pay a record of about 3.7 billion euros, including damages. UBS is appealing.

headline: Second crash: the 737 MAX is grounded worldwide
text: On 10 March an Ethiopian Airlines 737 MAX 8 crashed after take-off from Addis Ababa, killing all 157 on board, in circumstances similar to the Lion Air crash. China grounded the plane the next day, others followed, and on 13 March the US FAA became the last major regulator to ground it. Boeing's shares had their biggest fall since 2001.
imageCaption: Grounded Boeing 737 MAX jets parked near Boeing Field, Seattle, April 2019

headline: Nvidia buys Mellanox for 6.9 billion dollars
text: On 11 March Nvidia agreed to buy Mellanox Technologies, an Israeli maker of high-speed networking equipment for data centres and supercomputers, for 6.9 billion dollars.

headline: Disney+ will launch in November at 6.99 dollars
text: At an investor day on 11 April Disney announced that its streaming service Disney+ will launch in the United States on 12 November, for 6.99 dollars a month, with films and series from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars and National Geographic. The Fox purchase was completed last month.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B (read 2026-10-03; citing Variety, 11 April 2019, 'Disney+ to Launch in November, Priced at $6.99 Monthly')
imageCaption: The Disney+ home screen as Disney unveiled it to investors in Burbank, April 2019

headline: Microsoft is worth a trillion dollars
text: In April Microsoft became the third US listed company to be valued at more than one trillion dollars, as its cloud business keeps growing.
imageCaption: Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chief executive

headline: Alcon spun off
text: On 9 April Novartis completed the spin-off of its eye-care business Alcon: shareholders received Alcon shares, now listed on their own, and the new company is valued at about 28 billion francs. Novartis is now focused on medicines and generics.
imageCaption: Alcon's managers celebrate the first trade in the company's shares at SIX Swiss Exchange, Zurich, 9 April 2019

headline: Tariffs raised to 25%; Huawei blacklisted
text: Talks broke down and on 10 May the US raised tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods from 10% to 25%. Later in the month Washington restricted Huawei's access to American technology.

headline: Ola Källenius takes over as trade war worries hit car shares
text: Dieter Zetsche handed over to Ola Källenius on 22 May after 13 years as chief executive, and Daimler is restructuring its organisation. In May the US raised tariffs on Chinese goods and threatened Mexico with tariffs, hitting car shares worldwide. Daimler paid its dividend of 3.25 euros a share in May. Tesla fell 22% to a three-year low, hit harder than other car makers because it is building a factory in Shanghai and counts on selling many cars in China.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dieter_Zetsche (read 2026-10-03); electrive.com, 'Daimler restructures as Zetsche hands reins to Källenius', 22 May 2019 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); The Japan Times, 'Carmakers see $17 billion wiped out by Trump's Mexico threat', 1 June 2019 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); data/out/mercedes.json (dividend in May 2019) (read 2026-10-03); The Detroit News, 'Tesla hammered hardest by China tariff fears', 13 May 2019 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. imageCaption: Ola Källenius, Daimler chief executive from May 2019, at the Geneva motor show, April 2019

headline: Women's strike again, 28 years later
text: On 14 June an estimated 500,000 people joined a nationwide women's strike in Switzerland, the second after 1991, demanding equal pay, protection against harassment and more women in politics. Many wore purple and marched in Bern, Zurich, Basel, Geneva and Lausanne.
imageCaption: Women's strike march, Geneva, 14 June 2019

headline: The Fed cuts its rate for the first time since 2008
text: On 31 July the Fed lowered its interest rate by a quarter of a point, to a range of 2 to 2.25 percent. It is the first cut since December 2008, when the rate went to zero, and it comes after nine increases since 2015. The Fed speaks of insurance against a slowdown caused by trade disputes. The numbers: the Fed's rate 2.4 percent. Inflation 1.7 percent. Unemployment 3.6 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1955 to July 2019
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Oliver Zipse named chief executive
text: On 5 July BMW said Harald Krüger will not seek a second term, and on 18 July the supervisory board named the production chief Oliver Zipse as the new chairman of the board of management from 16 August. Mercedes has overtaken BMW as the best-selling luxury brand.
imageCaption: Oliver Zipse, member of the BMW board, named chief executive in July 2019

headline: IBM closes the Red Hat deal
text: IBM completed its 34 billion dollar purchase of Red Hat on 9 July, after the US Justice Department finished its review in May. Red Hat becomes part of IBM's hybrid cloud business.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hat (read 2026-10-03, citing Red Hat press release 2019-07-09); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arvind_Krishna (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Red Hat's headquarters, Raleigh, North Carolina

headline: Madoff's whistleblower calls GE 'a bigger fraud than Enron'
text: On 15 August Harry Markopolos, the investigator who exposed Bernard Madoff, accused General Electric of hiding 38 billion dollars of losses, mainly in long-term care insurance. GE denied any wrongdoing. The shares had their worst day in eleven years.
imageCaption: Harry Markopolos, the fraud investigator who warned the SEC about Bernard Madoff

headline: Cisco warns of flat sales
text: Cisco reported fiscal-year sales of $51.7 billion, up 7%, but forecast growth of only 0% to 2% for the coming quarter. Chief executive Chuck Robbins pointed to the long-term opportunity.

headline: Cobalt slump shuts Mutanda
text: Glencore's first-half adjusted EBITDA fell 32% to $5.6bn and net income to $226m. It will put its Mutanda copper and cobalt mine in Congo, which produced about a fifth of the world's cobalt in 2018, on care and maintenance by year-end because cobalt prices have collapsed, and booked a $350m cobalt loss in trading. Copper averaged $5,709 a tonne, its lowest in over two years.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/2019-half-year-report/5702770; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glencore (Mutanda 2018 output); https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/announcement-commodity-futures-trading-commission/5945728; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (all read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Mutanda copper and cobalt mine, Democratic Republic of the Congo

headline: Drones knock out half of Saudi output
text: Drone and missile attacks on 14 September hit Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq processing plant and the Khurais field, cutting 5.7 million barrels a day, about 5% of world supply. Brent futures jumped almost 20% on 16 September, the biggest jump since 1990, but Saudi Arabia moved quickly to restore output and prices gave back most of the gain.
imageCaption: Smoke rises from the Aramco oil facility at Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia, after the drone attacks, 14 September 2019

headline: A surprise profit, and a factory in Shanghai ahead of schedule
text: Wall Street expected Tesla to lose money again. Instead the company reported on 23 October a profit of 342 million dollars for the third quarter, on sales of 6.3 billion. It also said that its new factory near Shanghai, which it only began building early this year, has already started trial production, and that its next car, the Model Y, is ahead of schedule. The shares jumped about 20% the next day and gained 31% in October.
imageCaption: Gigafactory Shanghai, 2024

headline: Nokia stops its dividend to invest in 5G
text: On 24 October Nokia lowered its outlook for 2019 and 2020, citing pressure on margins from its first-generation 5G products, price competition in early 5G deals and problems in China, and decided not to pay the remaining dividend instalments for 2018 so it can invest more in 5G.
imageCaption: Rajeev Suri, Nokia's chief executive

headline: Altria writes down Juul by 4.5 billion dollars
text: On 31 October Altria wrote down the value of its Juul stake by 4.5 billion dollars, about 35% of what it paid ten months ago. Juul has stopped advertising and replaced its chief executive with an Altria executive amid a crisis over teenage vaping, and the House of Representatives is investigating the Altria deal.
imageCaption: A Juul e-cigarette ;;

headline: New boss, 11 billion dollar loss
text: Olivier Le Peuch, who became chief executive on 1 August in place of Paal Kibsgaard, reported on 18 October a third-quarter net loss of 11.38 billion dollars after charges of 8.65 dollars a share. Excluding charges, earnings per share rose 23 percent from the second quarter.
source: Schlumberger press release of 18 October 2019, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312519269681/ (read 2026-10-03); Schlumberger press release of 19 July 2019, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/000119312519197816/ (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: An oil pumpjack at work in Baku

headline: Disney+ starts streaming
text: Disney launched its streaming service Disney+ on 12 November in the United States, Canada and the Netherlands, with films and series from Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Star Wars. It plans to roll it out worldwide over the next two years.

headline: Petrol price protests crushed behind an internet blackout
text: After the government raised petrol prices by 50 to 200 percent overnight on 15 November, protests broke out across Iran. The authorities cut the internet almost entirely for about six days. Amnesty International said on 19 November that more than 100 protesters had been killed. Over 7,000 people have been arrested.
imageCaption: Fuel price protests in Iran, November 2019

headline: Ten million sign up for Disney+ on day one
text: Disney+ launched on 12 November in the United States, Canada and the Netherlands. A day later Disney said more than 10 million people had already signed up, despite log-in problems on the first day.
imageCaption: Bob Iger, Disney chief executive, 2019 ;;

headline: eBay sells StubHub for $4 billion
text: eBay agreed to sell StubHub, its ticket resale marketplace, to Viagogo for $4.05 billion in cash. Chief executive Devin Wenig left in September under pressure from the activist fund Elliott.

headline: McDonald's fires its CEO over a relationship with an employee
text: On 3 November McDonald's board dismissed chief executive Steve Easterbrook for a consensual relationship with an employee, which breaks company policy. Chris Kempczinski, president of McDonald's USA and a former PepsiCo and Kraft executive, became chief executive.
imageCaption: McDonald's chief executive Steve Easterbrook interviewed at the New York Stock Exchange, July 2017

headline: Novartis buys The Medicines Company
text: In late November Novartis agreed to buy The Medicines Company for $9.7 billion, $85 a share. It is Novartis's second big purchase under Narasimhan after AveXis.

headline: Siemens confirms the plan to spin off its energy business
text: On 7 November Siemens said it plans to carve out its Gas and Power division, add its 59% stake in Siemens Gamesa, and spin off and list the new Siemens Energy before the end of fiscal 2020. It expects earnings per share of 6.30 to 7.00 euros in fiscal 2020. Siemens shares rose 12% in November.
imageCaption: Siemens chief executive Joe Kaeser (left) with Argentina's president Mauricio Macri, Davos, January 2018

headline: 2019 in review: up 29 percent as the Fed cuts rates
text: The S&P 500 gained 29% in 2019 to 3,230.78, after first closing above 3,000 on 12 July, and the Dow 22.3%. The Federal Reserve cut its key rate three times, in July, September and October, to between 1.5 and 1.75 percent.

headline: Boeing halts MAX production and fires its CEO
text: On 16 December Boeing said it will suspend 737 MAX production in January, as the plane's return to service drags on. On 23 December the board dismissed chief executive Dennis Muilenburg and named chairman Dave Calhoun to replace him.
source: https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2019-12-16-Boeing-Statement-Regarding-737-MAX-Production (title seen in release list, 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_737_MAX_groundings (read 2026-10-03, citing Reuters 2019-12-23); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Boeing (read 2026-10-03, July 2019 charge)
imageCaption: Boeing chief executive Dennis Muilenburg testifying before the Senate Commerce Committee on the 737 MAX crashes, Washington, 29 October 2019

headline: Sony merges its phone, TV and camera businesses
text: During 2019 Sony merged its mobile phone, television and camera businesses into one unit. Sony's ADR rose about 40% this year.
